newsitem.title: UK: GNI cuts sharply 96/97 world cocoa deficit estimate.
newsitem.headline: GNI cuts sharply 96/97 world cocoa deficit estimate.

text.p: Commodity broker GNI Ltd has cut its estimate for world 1996/97 cocoa deficit to 33,000 tonnes from its previous forecast of 180,000 tonnes and compared with a surplus of 161,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
It said the new estimate was still well below its lower range forecast of 110,000 tonnes.
It revised upwards world production estimate to 2.718 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 2.56 million previously but still down from 1995/96's 2.856 million.
In its latest monthly Commodity Perspective report, GNI raised its forecast of the Ivorian crop to 1.15 million tonnes from 960,000 tonnes previously.
Main crop arrivals were close to 1.0 million tonnes and a mid-crop was expected in the region of 160,000 tonnes.
Future crops from Ivory Coast could be expected to surpass 1.2 million tonnes on a regular basis.
Only minor changes had been made to output from other producing countries, GNI said.
Cocoa consumption would rise to 2.751 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 2.739 million initially estimated, and up 2.1 percent from 1995/96's 2.69 million.
For 1997/98, GNI said the outlook also seemed rather sanguine.
Even with 4.0 percent consumption growth, expected improvements in Ivorian and Indonesian production were likely to produce only a modest deficit of just over 100,000 tonnes for 1997/98.
